description: Modernization tasks for PharmaBackend, generated from the .NET AppCAT assessment (report-20260619162917). Covers all four assessment categories: Configuration, Connection, Security, and Local URL reachability.

tasks.description: Externalize non-secret application settings to Azure App Configuration. Addresses issues: Local application configuration detected (Configuration.0003) in appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json (Logging:LogLevel, AllowedHosts, Seeding:ImageBaseUrl).
tasks.reason: The appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json files contain non-secret configuration that should be centrally managed in Azure App Configuration to enable dynamic refresh, environment-specific overrides, and controlled access without redeploying the application.
tasks.requirements: Move non-secret keys (Logging:LogLevel:*, AllowedHosts, Seeding:ImageBaseUrl) from appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json into Azure App Configuration. Preserve the existing IConfiguration / IOptions<T> shape so consumers do not need code changes. The Program.cs configuration pipeline already registers Azure App Configuration via DefaultAzureCredential and a Sentinel-based refresh trigger; reuse this setup. Keep secret-bearing keys (ConnectionStrings:*) out of App Configuration and route them through Key Vault references. Emit a .azure/configuration-migration.json seed file for the deployment agent.

tasks.description: Migrate the DefaultConnection (PostgreSQL via Npgsql) to Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server with passwordless Managed Identity authentication. Addresses issues: Connection string is detected (Connection.0001) for ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection in appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json.
tasks.reason: The application uses Entity Framework Core with Npgsql against a local PostgreSQL connection string. Migrating to Azure Database for PostgreSQL with Managed Identity removes the password from configuration, eliminates a credential rotation burden, and enables cloud-native HA/backup.
tasks.requirements: Replace the local PostgreSQL DefaultConnection with an Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server connection that authenticates via DefaultAzureCredential / Managed Identity. Update Entity Framework Core registration in Program.cs to acquire access tokens for the Azure Database for PostgreSQL audience and inject them into the Npgsql connection. Connection string parameters that must remain in configuration (Host, Database, Username) should be stored in Azure App Configuration; no password should be stored anywhere. Preserve existing AppDbContext, migrations, and health-check wiring. Verify EF Core migrations still apply against the Azure Database for PostgreSQL target.

tasks.description: Migrate the RedisConnection to Azure Cache for Redis with Managed Identity authentication via DefaultAzureCredential. Addresses issues: Connection string is detected (Connection.0001) for ConnectionStrings:RedisConnection in appsettings.json and appsettings.Development.json.
tasks.reason: The application uses StackExchange.Redis with a local Redis connection string and registers the cache via AddStackExchangeRedisCache. Migrating to Azure Cache for Redis with Managed Identity removes the access-key dependency and provides a managed, highly available distributed cache.
tasks.requirements: Replace the local RedisConnection with an Azure Cache for Redis instance using DefaultAzureCredential for token acquisition. Update the StackExchangeRedisCache registration in Program.cs to pass a ConfigurationOptions object that resolves the access token from Managed Identity, while preserving the existing InstanceName prefix and the AddRedis health-check tag. Store the Redis host endpoint in Azure App Configuration; do not store any access key or password. Ensure cache-aside read/write paths continue to function unchanged from a consumer perspective.

tasks.description: Move any remaining secret-bearing configuration into Azure Key Vault and consume it through Managed Identity. Addresses issues: Hardcoded sensitive data detected (Security.0003) flagged in Program.cs (lines 80 and 85).
tasks.reason: The .NET AppCAT scanner flagged occurrences of the literal 'secret' in Program.cs (lines 80 and 85). On manual review these are exception-message strings inside fail-fast guards (not real hardcoded secrets), and Program.cs already wires Azure Key Vault via DefaultAzureCredential. This task closes the gap by ensuring every secret value referenced by the application (Postgres credentials, Redis access token issuer config, any future API keys) lives only in Key Vault, and explicitly confirms there are no residual hardcoded credentials in source or configuration. This is mandatory severity when targeting Azure App Service Managed Instance on Windows.
tasks.requirements: Audit the source tree (Program.cs, appsettings*.json, Controllers, Services, Data) for any literal secret values (passwords, API keys, tokens, connection-string passwords, certificate thumbprints). For any found, move them into Azure Key Vault and reference them through either the existing AddAzureKeyVault pipeline or through Key Vault references in Azure App Configuration. Preserve the existing DefaultAzureCredential-based authentication flow already configured in Program.cs. Document Key Vault secret names and their consumers in .azure/configuration-migration.json. The two Program.cs incidents (lines 80, 85) are false positives — record them as reviewed-and-cleared in the task summary rather than rewriting the exception text.

tasks.description: Verify that the hardcoded image base URL in Data/DbSeeder.cs is reachable from Azure and ensure it is fully configurable. Addresses issues: Hardcoded URLs detected (Local.0006) at Data\DbSeeder.cs line 33.
tasks.reason: DbSeeder.cs falls back to the literal 'https://images.pexels.com/photos' when Seeding:ImageBaseUrl is not configured. Pexels is a public CDN reachable from Azure, but the fallback risks shipping a dev-only URL into production. The base URL is already configuration-driven (Seeding:ImageBaseUrl), so once that key is sourced from Azure App Configuration in task 001 the fallback should never be used in production.
tasks.requirements: Confirm that https://images.pexels.com/photos is reachable from the target Azure deployment region (it is a public HTTPS endpoint, so reachability is expected via normal egress). Ensure Seeding:ImageBaseUrl is always populated in production via Azure App Configuration (handled by task 001), and consider removing the hardcoded fallback in DbSeeder.cs or replacing it with a fail-fast guard so production seeds cannot silently use the Pexels CDN. No SDK changes are required; this is a verification and small hardening task.

tasks.description: Scan all PharmaBackend NuGet dependencies for known CVEs and remediate any identified vulnerabilities at or above the assessment minimum severity (high).
tasks.reason: The assessment was generated with minimumCveSeverity=high. Before promoting the modernized application to Azure, all dependencies (including any new Azure SDK packages introduced by the transform tasks) must be free of known high/critical CVEs.
tasks.requirements: Run a CVE scan over all NuGet packages referenced by PharmacyBackend.csproj after the transform tasks have introduced their Azure SDK dependencies (Azure.Identity, Azure.Extensions.AspNetCore.Configuration.Secrets, Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.AzureAppConfiguration, Azure.Security.KeyVault.Secrets, Microsoft.Azure.StackExchangeRedis, Azure.Identity-aware Npgsql token providers, etc.). Upgrade each vulnerable package to the minimum patched version that still satisfies the project's target framework (net10.0). If a fix requires a major version upgrade, document the affected dependency, current version, target major version, and breaking-change risk in the task summary. After remediation, run dotnet build and dotnet test and confirm both pass.
